subject: Maths
question: What is the smallest number written using only the digit 4 (4, 44, 444, ...) that is divisible by 12?
solution: 12 = 4 × 3. Any such number from 44 on ends in 44, which is divisible by 4. For 3 the digit sum 4 × (number of 4s) must be a multiple of 3, so three 4s are needed: 444 = 12 × 37.
questionHi: केवल अंक 4 से लिखी (4, 44, 444, ...) वह सबसे छोटी संख्या कौन-सी है जो 12 से विभाज्य हो?
solutionHi: 12 = 4 × 3। 44 से आगे हर ऐसी संख्या 44 पर समाप्त होती है, जो 4 से विभाज्य है। 3 के लिए अंकों का योग 4 × (4 की संख्या), 3 का गुणज हो, अतः तीन 4 चाहिए: 444 = 12 × 37।

question: For how many choices of the digits a and b is the six-digit number a1234b divisible by 36?
solution: 36 = 4 × 9. For 4 the last two digits 4b must be divisible by 4: b = 0, 4 or 8. For 9 the digit sum a + b + 10 must be 18 or 27, so a + b = 8 or 17. b = 0 gives a = 8; b = 4 gives a = 4; b = 8 gives a = 9 (a = 0 is not allowed as the first digit). So 3 choices.
questionHi: अंकों a और b के कितने चयनों के लिए छह अंकों की संख्या a1234b, 36 से विभाज्य है?
solutionHi: 36 = 4 × 9। 4 के लिए अंतिम दो अंक 4b, 4 से विभाज्य हों: b = 0, 4 या 8। 9 के लिए अंकों का योग a + b + 10, 18 या 27 हो, अतः a + b = 8 या 17। b = 0 से a = 8; b = 4 से a = 4; b = 8 से a = 9 (पहला अंक a = 0 नहीं हो सकता)। अतः 3 चयन।

question: What is the largest power of 3 that divides 100!?
solution: Count the factors of 3: 100 ÷ 3 gives 33 multiples of 3, 100 ÷ 9 gives 11 multiples of 9, 100 ÷ 27 gives 3 multiples of 27 and 100 ÷ 81 gives 1. 33 + 11 + 3 + 1 = 48, so 3⁴⁸.

question: For every natural number n, n⁵ − n is divisible by:
solution: n⁵ − n = (n − 1)n(n + 1)(n² + 1). Three consecutive numbers give factors 2 and 3. For 5: if n leaves 0, 1 or 4 on division by 5, one of n, n − 1, n + 1 is a multiple of 5; if it leaves 2 or 3, n² + 1 is. So 30 always divides it. n = 2 gives 30 itself, so 60, 25 and 20 do not.
questionHi: प्रत्येक प्राकृत संख्या n के लिए n⁵ − n किससे विभाज्य है?
solutionHi: n⁵ − n = (n − 1)n(n + 1)(n² + 1)। तीन क्रमागत संख्याओं से 2 और 3 मिलते हैं। 5 के लिए: यदि n का 5 से शेष 0, 1 या 4 हो तो n, n − 1, n + 1 में से एक 5 का गुणज; यदि 2 या 3 हो तो n² + 1। अतः 30 सदा विभाजित करता है। n = 2 पर मान 30 ही है, अतः 60, 25 और 20 नहीं।

subject: Maths
question: How many numbers from 1 to 1,000 are divisible by 6 or by 10, but not by 15?
solution: Multiples of 6: 166, of 10: 100, of both (that is, of 30): 33, so 166 + 100 − 33 = 233 are divisible by 6 or 10. Such a number is divisible by 15 only if it is a multiple of 30: 33 of them. 233 − 33 = 200.

question: What is the smallest number that is divisible by 7 and leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by each of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6?
solution: The LCM of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 is 60, so the number is 60k + 1: 61, 121, 181, 241, 301, ... On division by 7 these leave 5, 2, 6, 3, 0. The first multiple of 7 is 301 = 7 × 43.
questionHi: वह सबसे छोटी संख्या कौन-सी है जो 7 से विभाज्य है और 2, 3, 4, 5 तथा 6 में से प्रत्येक से भाग देने पर 1 शेष छोड़ती है?

subject: Maths
question: How many five-digit numbers that use each of the digits 0, 1, 2, 3 and 6 exactly once are divisible by 12?
solution: The digits add to 12, so every such number is divisible by 3; it must also be divisible by 4. Possible last two digits: 12, 16, 20, 32, 36, 60. For 20 and 60 the other three digits (no 0 among them) can be arranged in 3! = 6 ways each: 12. For 12, 16, 32 and 36 the other three include 0, which cannot lead: 6 − 2 = 4 ways each: 16. Total 28.
questionHi: अंकों 0, 1, 2, 3 और 6 में से हर एक को ठीक एक बार प्रयोग करने वाली पाँच अंकों की कितनी संख्याएँ 12 से विभाज्य हैं?
solutionHi: अंकों का योग 12, अतः हर ऐसी संख्या 3 से विभाज्य; 4 से भी विभाज्य होनी चाहिए। संभव अंतिम दो अंक: 12, 16, 20, 32, 36, 60। 20 और 60 के लिए बाकी तीन अंक (उनमें 0 नहीं) 3! = 6 तरह से: 12। 12, 16, 32 और 36 के लिए बाकी तीन में 0 है, जो आगे नहीं आ सकता: 6 − 2 = 4 तरह से: 16। कुल 28।

question: For every natural number n, 3²ⁿ⁺¹ + 2ⁿ⁺² is divisible by:
solution: 3²ⁿ⁺¹ + 2ⁿ⁺² = 3 × 9ⁿ + 4 × 2ⁿ. 9 = 7 + 2, so 9ⁿ leaves the same remainder as 2ⁿ on division by 7, and the sum leaves the same as 3 × 2ⁿ + 4 × 2ⁿ = 7 × 2ⁿ, i.e. 0. n = 1 gives 35 and n = 2 gives 259 = 7 × 37, so 5, 11 and 13 fail.

question: How many two-digit numbers with no 0 among their digits are divisible by each of their own digits?
solution: The nine numbers with equal digits (11, 22, ..., 99) all work. Of the rest, only 12, 15, 24, 36 and 48 are divisible by both digits. 9 + 5 = 14.
questionHi: जिनमें कोई अंक 0 नहीं है, ऐसी दो अंकों की कितनी संख्याएँ अपने प्रत्येक अंक से विभाज्य हैं?

subject: Maths
question: For how many digits a is the eight-digit number 1a1a1a1a divisible by 99?
solution: For 11 the alternate sums are 4 (the four 1s) and 4a (the four a's): 4a − 4 must be a multiple of 11, which only a = 1 gives. But 11,111,111 has digit sum 8, not a multiple of 9. So no digit works: 0.
questionHi: कितने अंकों a के लिए आठ अंकों की संख्या 1a1a1a1a, 99 से विभाज्य है?
solutionHi: 11 के लिए एकांतर योग 4 (चार 1) और 4a (चार a): 4a − 4, 11 का गुणज हो, जो केवल a = 1 से होता है। पर 11,111,111 के अंकों का योग 8, जो 9 का गुणज नहीं। अतः कोई अंक नहीं: 0।

question: What is the largest number that always divides the product of any four consecutive odd numbers?
solution: Among four consecutive odd numbers one is always a multiple of 3 (odd numbers run through the remainders 1, 0, 2 on division by 3). Nothing else is forced: 1 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 105, 7 × 9 × 11 × 13 = 9,009 and 9 × 11 × 13 × 15 = 19,305 have HCF 3. So 3.

subject: Maths
question: How many perfect cubes from 1 to 10,000 are divisible by 6?
solution: n³ is divisible by 2 only if n is, and by 3 only if n is, so n must be a multiple of 6. The cubes up to 10,000 are 1³ to 21³ (21³ = 9,261), and the multiples of 6 there are 6, 12 and 18: 3 cubes.
questionHi: 1 से 10,000 तक कितने पूर्ण घन 6 से विभाज्य हैं?
solutionHi: n³, 2 से तभी विभाज्य जब n हो, और 3 से तभी जब n हो, अतः n, 6 का गुणज हो। 10,000 तक के घन 1³ से 21³ (21³ = 9,261), और उनमें 6 के गुणज 6, 12 और 18: 3 घन।

subject: Maths
question: What is the largest number that always divides n(n + 1)(2n + 1) for every natural number n?
solution: n and n + 1 give a factor 2. One of n, n + 1, 2n + 1 is a multiple of 3: if n leaves 0 on division by 3, n is; if it leaves 2, n + 1 is; if it leaves 1, 2n + 1 is. So 6 always divides it, and n = 1 gives 1 × 2 × 3 = 6 itself, so nothing larger does.
questionHi: वह सबसे बड़ी संख्या कौन-सी है जो प्रत्येक प्राकृत संख्या n के लिए n(n + 1)(2n + 1) को सदा विभाजित करती है?
solutionHi: n और n + 1 से गुणनखंड 2 मिलता है। n, n + 1, 2n + 1 में से एक 3 का गुणज है (यदि n का 3 से शेष 1 हो, तो 2n + 1 का शेष 2 × 1 + 1 = 3, यानी 0)। अतः 6 सदा विभाजित करता है, और n = 1 पर 1 × 2 × 3 = 6 ही है, अतः इससे बड़ी कोई नहीं।

question: By what smallest number must 2⁶ × 3⁵ × 5⁴ be multiplied so that the product is divisible by 6⁷?
solution: 6⁷ = 2⁷ × 3⁷. The number has 2⁶ and 3⁵, so it is short of one 2 and two 3s: multiply by 2 × 3² = 18.
questionHi: 2⁶ × 3⁵ × 5⁴ को किस सबसे छोटी संख्या से गुणा करें कि गुणनफल 6⁷ से विभाज्य हो?
solutionHi: 6⁷ = 2⁷ × 3⁷। संख्या में 2⁶ और 3⁵ हैं, अतः एक 2 और दो 3 कम हैं: 2 × 3² = 18 से गुणा करें।

question: The three-digit number 2a3 is added to 326 to give the three-digit number 5b9. If 5b9 is divisible by 9, what is a + b?
solution: 2a3 + 326 = 5b9 means b = a + 2 (no carry from the units, 3 + 6 = 9). For 9 the digit sum 5 + b + 9 = 14 + b must be 18, so b = 4 and a = 2. a + b = 6 (223 + 326 = 549 = 9 × 61).
questionHi: तीन अंकों की संख्या 2a3 को 326 में जोड़ने पर तीन अंकों की संख्या 5b9 मिलती है। यदि 5b9, 9 से विभाज्य है, तो a + b का मान क्या है?

question: For how many natural numbers n from 1 to 90 is n² + 3n + 2 divisible by 6?
solution: n² + 3n + 2 = (n + 1)(n + 2), two consecutive numbers, so it is always even. It is divisible by 3 unless n is itself a multiple of 3 (then neither n + 1 nor n + 2 is). From 1 to 90 there are 30 multiples of 3, so 90 − 30 = 60.
questionHi: 1 से 90 तक कितनी प्राकृत संख्याओं n के लिए n² + 3n + 2, 6 से विभाज्य है?
solutionHi: n² + 3n + 2 = (n + 1)(n + 2), दो क्रमागत संख्याएँ, अतः सदा सम। यह 3 से विभाज्य है, सिवाय जब n स्वयं 3 का गुणज हो (तब न n + 1, न n + 2)। 1 से 90 में 3 के 30 गुणज, अतः 90 − 30 = 60।

question: If the five-digit number 653xy is divisible by 80, what is the value of x + y?
solution: 80 = 16 × 5. For 5 and 2, y = 0. Then 653x0 = 10 × 653x, so 653x must be divisible by 8: among 6,530 to 6,539 only 6,536 = 8 × 817 is. x = 6, y = 0, x + y = 6.

question: For how many choices of the digits a, b and c is the five-digit number 4a5bc divisible by 125?
solution: A number is divisible by 125 when its last three digits are: 000, 125, 250, 375, 500, 625, 750 or 875. Here they are 5bc, so only 500 fits: b = c = 0. The digit a is free: 10 choices.

question: For every natural number n, 7²ⁿ − 4²ⁿ is divisible by:
solution: 7²ⁿ − 4²ⁿ = 49ⁿ − 16ⁿ, and aⁿ − bⁿ is always divisible by a − b = 49 − 16 = 33. n = 1 gives 33 itself, so 65, 13 and 9 do not always divide it.
questionHi: प्रत्येक प्राकृत संख्या n के लिए 7²ⁿ − 4²ⁿ किससे विभाज्य है?

question: What is the smallest natural number which, multiplied by 7, gives a number written only with the digit 5?
solution: We need the smallest number 55...5 divisible by 7. 5, 55, 555, 5,555 and 55,555 leave 5, 6, 2, 4 and 6 on division by 7; 555,555 = 5 × 111,111 = 5 × 7 × 15,873 is the first. 555,555 ÷ 7 = 79,365.

subject: Maths
question: What is the smallest number written using only the digit 2 (2, 22, 222, ...) that is divisible by 24?
solution: 24 = 8 × 3, and a number is divisible by 8 only if its last three digits are. From 222 on, every such number ends in 222 = 8 × 27 + 6, and 2 and 22 are not multiples of 8 either. So none of them is divisible by 8, let alone 24: No such number.
questionHi: केवल अंक 2 से लिखी (2, 22, 222, ...) वह सबसे छोटी संख्या कौन-सी है जो 24 से विभाज्य हो?
solutionHi: 24 = 8 × 3, और कोई संख्या 8 से तभी विभाज्य जब उसके अंतिम तीन अंक हों। 222 से आगे हर ऐसी संख्या 222 = 8 × 27 + 6 पर समाप्त होती है, और 2 तथा 22 भी 8 के गुणज नहीं। अतः कोई भी 8 से विभाज्य नहीं, 24 से तो दूर: ऐसी कोई संख्या नहीं।

question: For how many choices of the digits a and b is the six-digit number 2a5b84 divisible by 132?
solution: 132 = 4 × 3 × 11. The last two digits 84 make it divisible by 4. For 11 the alternate sums are (4 + b + a) and (8 + 5 + 2) = 15, so a + b − 11 must be a multiple of 11: a + b = 11. Then the digit sum is 19 + 11 = 30, divisible by 3. a + b = 11 has 8 solutions (a from 2 to 9).

question: What is the largest power of 10 that divides 300!?
solution: Each 10 needs a 2 and a 5, and 5s are the scarcer. Factors of 5 in 300!: 300 ÷ 5 = 60, 300 ÷ 25 = 12, 300 ÷ 125 = 2. 60 + 12 + 2 = 74, so 10⁷⁴.

question: What is the largest number that divides n³ − n for every odd natural number n?
solution: n³ − n = (n − 1)n(n + 1). For odd n, n − 1 and n + 1 are consecutive even numbers, one of them a multiple of 4, so their product is divisible by 8; and one of the three consecutive numbers is a multiple of 3. So 24 divides it, and n = 3 gives 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 itself.
questionHi: वह सबसे बड़ी संख्या कौन-सी है जो प्रत्येक विषम प्राकृत संख्या n के लिए n³ − n को विभाजित करती है?
solutionHi: n³ − n = (n − 1)n(n + 1)। विषम n के लिए n − 1 और n + 1 क्रमागत सम संख्याएँ हैं, उनमें एक 4 का गुणज, अतः गुणनफल 8 से विभाज्य; और तीन क्रमागत संख्याओं में एक 3 का गुणज। अतः 24 विभाजित करता है, और n = 3 पर 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 ही।

subject: Maths
question: How many numbers from 1 to 1,000 are divisible by exactly one of 4 and 6?
solution: Multiples of 4: 250; of 6: 166; of both (that is, of 12): 83. Exactly one: (250 − 83) + (166 − 83) = 167 + 83 = 250.

question: What is the least number that must be subtracted from 1,000,000 to make it divisible by 7, 11 and 13?
solution: Divisible by 7, 11 and 13 means divisible by 7 × 11 × 13 = 1,001. 999 × 1,001 = 999,999, so 1,000,000 leaves 1: subtract 1.

subject: Maths
question: How many four-digit numbers with all digits different can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 that are divisible by 25?
solution: A number is divisible by 25 when it ends in 00, 25, 50 or 75. Without 0 and 7 only 25 is possible. The first two places take two of the remaining four digits in order: 4 × 3 = 12.
questionHi: अंकों 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 और 6 से भिन्न अंकों वाली चार अंकों की कितनी संख्याएँ बन सकती हैं जो 25 से विभाज्य हों?
solutionHi: कोई संख्या 25 से तब विभाज्य जब वह 00, 25, 50 या 75 पर समाप्त हो। 0 और 7 के बिना केवल 25 संभव। पहले दो स्थानों पर बचे चार में से दो अंक क्रम से: 4 × 3 = 12।

question: For every natural number n, 11ⁿ⁺² + 12²ⁿ⁺¹ is divisible by:
solution: 11ⁿ⁺² + 12²ⁿ⁺¹ = 121 × 11ⁿ + 12 × 144ⁿ. 144 = 133 + 11, so 144ⁿ leaves the same remainder as 11ⁿ on division by 133, and the sum leaves the same as 121 × 11ⁿ + 12 × 11ⁿ = 133 × 11ⁿ, i.e. 0. n = 1 gives 3,059 = 133 × 23, which 121, 143 and 169 do not divide.

question: A two-digit number minus the number formed by reversing its digits is 45. How many such two-digit numbers are there?
solution: 10a + b − (10b + a) = 9(a − b) = 45, so a − b = 5: 50, 61, 72, 83 and 94 (50 reversed is 05 = 5, and 50 − 5 = 45). That is 5 numbers.

subject: Maths
question: Which of 3,553, 3,563, 4,673 and 5,729 is divisible by 19?
solution: Test for 19: add twice the last digit to the rest. 3,553 → 355 + 6 = 361 = 19 × 19, so 3,553 = 19 × 187 is divisible. 3,563 → 356 + 6 = 362, 4,673 → 467 + 6 = 473, 5,729 → 572 + 18 = 590, none a multiple of 19.

subject: Maths
question: For how many natural numbers n from 1 to 60 is 2ⁿ − 1 divisible by 9?
solution: Powers of 2 on division by 9 leave 2, 4, 8, 7, 5, 1 and then repeat every 6. So 2ⁿ − 1 is divisible by 9 exactly when n is a multiple of 6: 6, 12, ..., 60, that is 10 values.
questionHi: 1 से 60 तक कितनी प्राकृत संख्याओं n के लिए 2ⁿ − 1, 9 से विभाज्य है?
solutionHi: 9 से भाग पर 2 की घातों के शेष 2, 4, 8, 7, 5, 1 और फिर हर 6 पर दोहराव। अतः 2ⁿ − 1, 9 से तभी विभाज्य जब n, 6 का गुणज हो: 6, 12, ..., 60, यानी 10 मान।

subject: Maths
question: Which of the following divides the product 1 × 3 × 5 × 7 × ... × 99 of all odd numbers from 1 to 99?
solution: The product is odd, so 100, 98 and 64 (all even) cannot divide it. 225 = 9 × 25 = 3² × 5², and the product contains 3 and 9 (two more 3s) and 5 and 25 (more than two 5s). So 225.

question: What is the largest number that always divides n²(n² − 1) for every natural number n?
solution: n²(n² − 1) = n × (n − 1)n(n + 1). The three consecutive numbers give 3. For 4: if n is even, n² is a multiple of 4; if n is odd, (n − 1)(n + 1) is a multiple of 8. So 12 always divides it, and n = 2 gives 4 × 3 = 12 itself.
